title: What entry-level driver training does FMCSA require before a CDL skills test?
description: What 49 CFR Part 380 Subpart F requires of CDL applicants and training providers since February 7, 2022, including the Training Provider Registry.
shortAnswer: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) requires anyone applying for a first Class A or Class B commercial driver's license (CDL), upgrading to Class A or B, or seeking a first passenger, school bus or hazardous materials endorsement to complete entry-level driver training from a provider listed on the Training Provider Registry. The rule is 49 CFR Part 380 Subpart F, in force since February 7, 2022. Theory training requires an 80 percent assessment score.
keyTakeaways: Entry-level driver training (ELDT) applies to individuals seeking a first Class A or B CDL, an upgrade to Class A or B, or a first P, S or H endorsement (49 CFR 380.609).

Training must come from a provider listed on FMCSA's Training Provider Registry (TPR), and the provider must certify completion through the TPR by midnight of the second business day after training ends (49 CFR 380.717).

There are no minimum classroom or behind-the-wheel hours: the curriculum in Appendices A to E must be covered in full, theory knowledge must be assessed with an overall score of at least 80 percent, and BTW proficiency must be documented.
States may not run the CDL skills test (or, for the H endorsement, the knowledge test) until ELDT completion is verified (49 CFR 383.73).
Training providers must keep assessment records, lesson plans and instructor qualification evidence for at least three years (49 CFR 380.725).
regulator: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), U.S. Department of Transportation
appliesTo: Individuals applying for a Class A or Class B CDL for the first time, or upgrading to Class A or Class B
Individuals seeking a passenger (P), school bus (S) or hazardous materials (H) endorsement for the first time
Training providers, including motor carriers, schools, unions and individuals, that deliver theory or behind-the-wheel ELDT
Motor carriers that run in-house CDL programs or sponsor trainees through external schools

sections.heading: What does the ELDT rule require?

blocks.text: The rule requires entry-level drivers to complete a federally defined theory curriculum and, for Class A, Class B, passenger and school bus credentials, a behind-the-wheel (BTW) curriculum, delivered by a registered provider before the state will test them. [49 CFR 380.601](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.601) says Subpart F "establishes training requirements for entry-level drivers" and minimum content for theory and BTW curricula, and that it applies only to people who apply for a CDL, a CDL upgrade or an endorsement.

The operative requirement is in [49 CFR 380.609](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.609): an individual who applies "for the first time, for a Class A or Class B CDL, or who upgrades to a Class A or B CDL, must complete driver training from a provider listed on the Training Provider Registry (TPR)". A parallel paragraph applies the same requirement to a first passenger, school bus or hazardous materials endorsement.

FMCSA published the final rule, Minimum Training Requirements for Entry-Level Commercial Motor Vehicle Operators, in the [Federal Register on December 8, 2016](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2016/12/08/2016-28012/minimum-training-requirements-for-entry-level-commercial-motor-vehicle-operators). After later amendments delayed the compliance date, the subpart has applied on and after February 7, 2022, as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Who must complete entry-level driver training, and who is exempt?

blocks.text: ELDT applies to entry-level drivers who intend to drive commercial motor vehicles in interstate or intrastate commerce, which FMCSA defines by reference to the CDL skills test: an entry-level driver is someone who must pass the skills test under 49 CFR 383.71 to get a first CDL, upgrade to Class A or B, or obtain a first H, P or S endorsement.
[49 CFR 380.603](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.603) lists the exceptions and transition rules:

items: **Grandfathered credentials:** drivers issued a Class A or B CDL, or a P, S or H endorsement, before February 7, 2022 do not need ELDT for that credential.

**Commercial learner's permit (CLP) timing:** a person who obtained a CLP before February 7, 2022 is exempt if they get the CDL before the CLP or renewed CLP expires. Anyone who obtained a CLP on or after that date must comply.

**Excepted drivers:** drivers excepted from CDL requirements under 49 CFR 383.3(c), (d) and (h), applicants for restricted CDLs under 383.3(e) to (g), qualifying military personnel under 383.77, and drivers removing a restriction under 383.135(b)(7).
**Completion window:** except for the H endorsement, the theory and BTW (range and public road) portions must be completed within one year of completing the first portion.

blocks.text: ELDT is a licensing prerequisite, not an employer refresher. It does not replace the function specific hazmat employee training an employer owes under [49 CFR 172.704](/regulations/dot-hazmat-employee-training), even where a driver also holds the H endorsement.

sections.heading: How many hours of training are required, and how is it assessed?

blocks.text: No minimum number of hours is required for either theory or BTW training. Appendix A to Part 380 states that "there is no required minimum number of instruction hours for theory training, but the training instructor must cover all topics set forth in the curriculum", and says the same for BTW range and public road training.

Instead of hours, the rule sets content and a pass standard. The curricula are in five appendices: [Appendix A](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/part-380/appendix-Appendix%20A%20to%20Part%20380) for Class A, Appendix B for Class B, Appendix C for the passenger endorsement, Appendix D for the school bus endorsement and Appendix E for the hazardous materials endorsement. Class B holders upgrading to Class A may take a shorter theory upgrade curriculum.

Under [49 CFR 380.715](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.715), providers must use written assessments of the knowledge objectives in each theory unit, and "the driver-trainee must receive an overall minimum score of 80 percent on the theory assessment". For BTW, instructors must evaluate and document proficiency against the curriculum, and Appendix A adds that a simulation device cannot be used for BTW range or public road training or to demonstrate proficiency. Instructors must also document the total BTW clock hours each trainee spends, even though no minimum applies.

blocks.title: Proficiency, not seat time
blocks.text: Because the rule sets no minimum hours, an auditor of a training provider will look for evidence that every curriculum topic was covered and that each trainee demonstrated each BTW element. A completion certificate without unit level assessment records will not show that.

sections.heading: What must a provider do to be listed on the Training Provider Registry?

blocks.text: A provider must meet curriculum, facility, vehicle and instructor criteria, hold any state authorization required where it trains in person, accept FMCSA audits, and register each campus online to get a unique TPR number. These conditions are set out in [49 CFR 380.703](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.703).

items: **Instructors:** theory and BTW instructors must hold a CDL of the same or higher class with the needed endorsements and have at least two years of experience driving that class of vehicle or as a BTW instructor, plus any state instructor qualifications ([49 CFR 380.605](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.605)). An instructor whose CDL was disqualified under 383.51 may not give BTW instruction for two years after reinstatement.

**Applicant checks:** providers must verify that BTW applicants hold a valid CLP or CDL and have them certify they will comply with DOT rules on drug and alcohol testing, age, medical certification, licensing and driving record ([49 CFR 380.707](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.707)).
**Split delivery:** separate providers may deliver theory and BTW, but range and public road BTW must come from the same provider.

**Certification:** after training, the provider must transmit the trainee's details, credential, training type, BTW clock hours, TPR number and completion dates through the TPR by midnight of the second business day ([49 CFR 380.717](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.717)).

**Continued listing:** providers must update their registration biennially, report key changes within 30 days, and produce required documentation within 48 hours of an FMCSA request ([49 CFR 380.719](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.719)).

blocks.text: FMCSA may remove a provider from the registry for failing these conditions, refusing an audit, material deficiencies, or false claims of state licensure, and it may consider its trainees' skills test pass rates. Training delivered after a removal date is treated as invalid, and in cases of fraud in which trainees knowingly took part, FMCSA may invalidate training retroactively ([49 CFR 380.721](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.721)).

sections.heading: How do states check that ELDT was completed?

blocks.text: States check electronically through the TPR before testing. Under [49 CFR 383.73](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-383.73), beginning on February 7, 2022 a state may not conduct a skills test for a Class A or B CDL or a P or S endorsement until it "verifies electronically that the applicant completed the training prescribed in subpart F of part 380". For the H endorsement the check sits before the knowledge test, because hazardous materials ELDT is theory only.

In practice this makes the provider's certification upload the gate on the trainee's test date. A late or incorrect TPR submission delays licensing, which is why carriers with in-house schools treat the two business day deadline as an operational control rather than an administrative task.

sections.heading: How can carriers and schools map ELDT obligations to evidence?

blocks.text: For a carrier running an in-house CDL school, each ELDT duty lands on either the trainee or the provider, at a defined point in the training cycle, and leaves a specific record behind. This planning aid, compiled from the regulatory text rather than issued by FMCSA, lines those up.

blocks.text: Carriers that combine ELDT with company onboarding can use the same structure for their wider [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix), so licensing prerequisites, drug and alcohol education under [49 CFR Part 382](/regulations/dot-drug-and-alcohol-supervisor-training) and hazmat function training sit in one record per driver.

sections.heading: What records must training providers keep, and has the rule changed recently?

blocks.text: Providers must keep applicant self certifications, copies of CLPs or CDLs, instructor qualification records, theory and BTW lesson plans, and individual assessment records for a minimum of three years from the date each record is generated or received ([49 CFR 380.725](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-380.725)). Longer state or other federal retention periods still apply.

As at November 2026 the substantive ELDT requirements have not changed since the 2022 compliance date; the most recent amendments to Subpart G date from September 2022. FMCSA continues to process individual exemption applications, and on [October 21, 2026](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/21/2026-21514/agency-information-collection-activities-renewal-of-an-approved-information-collection-training) it gave notice that it intends to renew the TPR information collection, estimating 26,284 training provider respondents and seeking approval to continue collecting certification data until 2030. Providers should check the eCFR and FMCSA notices before each curriculum review, as described in [how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each Appendix A to E unit and BTW element to a defined learning outcome and an assessment point before any course material is written, so an 80 percent theory score can be traced back to the knowledge objectives it is meant to test. The same framework holds instructor qualification and retention requirements, so a provider can show an auditor how curriculum, assessment and records connect.

faqs.q: Can ELDT theory training be completed online?
faqs.a: Yes. Theory instruction may be delivered through online training, computer based instruction, lectures or similar means, as long as the content is prepared or delivered by a qualified theory instructor. State qualification requirements for theory instruction do not apply to providers that offer theory only online. BTW training cannot be done on a simulator.

faqs.q: Does ELDT apply to a Class B driver upgrading to Class A?
faqs.a: Yes. Upgrading to a Class A CDL triggers ELDT under 49 CFR 380.609. A Class B holder may complete the Class A theory upgrade curriculum instead of the standard theory curriculum, but still needs the Class A BTW training from a registered provider before the state will administer the skills test.

faqs.q: Can a motor carrier train its own drivers for a CDL?
faqs.a: Yes, if it registers on the Training Provider Registry and meets the same curriculum, instructor, facility, vehicle, assessment and record keeping requirements as any other provider. Each campus or training location needs its own TPR registration and number.

faqs.q: Is there a refresher requirement under the ELDT rule?
faqs.a: No. ELDT is a one time prerequisite tied to a specific CDL class or endorsement. Ongoing obligations come from other rules, such as hazmat employee recurrent training at least every three years and drug and alcohol education under Part 382, which carriers manage separately.
